title: Correct and harden the HTTP transport
description:
Make the transport standards-aware and predictable using a deterministic local HTTP harness. Correct URL/query construction, header normalization, raw and form bodies, cancellation ownership, redirect handling, decompression, charset decoding, binary preservation, timing, and error reporting.

Redirects must apply method/body rules deliberately, enforce a hop limit, resolve relative locations, and strip authorization, cookies, and other sensitive headers on cross-origin hops. Each execution owns its own AbortController; cancellation must not affect another request. Decode supported content encodings before text conversion, honor declared charsets when feasible, and return binary content as exact base64 with the response MIME type.

Enforce a configurable response limit with a 10 MiB default and allowed range of 1 KiB to 100 MiB. Fail with typed, user-actionable errors for timeout, cancellation, DNS/TLS/socket failures, malformed redirects, decompression, and size overflow. Cover all methods and body modes in automated tests.

checklist.text: Build a deterministic local server harness for methods, bodies, redirects, compression, encodings, delays, and oversized responses
Normalize URL/query/header construction and encode raw, urlencoded, multipart, and empty bodies correctly
Give each execution an isolated AbortController and distinguish user cancellation from timeout
Implement bounded redirects with correct method/body transitions and cross-origin credential stripping
Decompress supported encodings, decode text by charset, and preserve exact binary bytes and MIME type
Enforce the configurable 10 MiB default response limit within the approved 1 KiB to 100 MiB range
Return typed secret-safe errors and accurate DNS/connect/TLS/first-byte/download/total timing where observable
Test methods, query edge cases, all bodies, redirects, auth stripping, cancellation, timeout, compression, charset, binary, and limits
